title: One Point Lesson - Gearbox Oil Level & Change (ISO VG 220) (OPL-CT-7801-02)
content:
ONE POINT LESSON (OPL): OPL-CT-7801-02 - Gearbox Oil Level & Change (ISO VG 220).

Equipment: CT-7801 (COOLING TOWER CELL FAN), Discipline: Mechanical, Area: 7800 - COOLING TOWER SYSTEM.

Related Interlock: SEQ-7801 (SIL 1), P&ID: TJC-LLD-PID-7801.

PURPOSE & OBJECTIVE:
This One Point Lesson explains gearbox oil level & change (iso vg 220) for CT-7801 (COOLING TOWER CELL FAN) in the COOLING TOWER SYSTEM. Low or degraded gearbox oil causes overheating (TSHH-7803) and gear failure high up on the fan deck. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the correct step-by-step method so the task is done safely, correctly and consistently every time.

SAFETY PRECAUTIONS:
- Precaution 1: Apply LOTO (Lock-Out Tag-Out) and prove zero energy before starting work.
- Precaution 2: Isolate, depressurise, drain and purge the equipment; obtain a valid work permit.
- Precaution 3: Wear the correct PPE: coverall, safety shoes, gloves, goggles and hearing protection.
- Precaution 4: Beware of stored mechanical energy (springs, rotating inertia) and pinch points.
- Precaution 5: Use certified lifting gear and correct manual-handling technique for heavy parts.

TOOLS & MATERIALS:
- Tool 1: Standard mechanical hand tools & calibrated torque wrench
- Tool 2: LOTO padlocks and permit
- Tool 3: Laser/dial alignment kit (as applicable)
- Tool 4: Feeler gauges, dial indicator, seal/bearing pullers
- Tool 5: Correct spare parts and gaskets per the BOM
- Tool 6: Lifting gear and slings (certified)

STEP-BY-STEP PROCEDURE:
- Step 1 - Action: Check the gearbox sight-glass oil level
- Step 1 - Check: Isolation & LOTO verified
- Step 2 - Action: Sample the oil for water contamination and metal
- Step 2 - Check: Parts match BOM / spec
- Step 3 - Action: Change the ISO VG 220 (4.5 L) per the schedule
- Step 3 - Check: Torque / clearance to spec
- Step 4 - Action: Verify the oil pressure PSL-7807 after refill
- Step 4 - Check: No leak / smooth operation
- Step 5 - Action: Record the oil change and next due date
- Step 5 - Check: Record in equipment history

COMMON PROBLEMS & TROUBLESHOOTING:
- Symptom: Scheduled fan gearbox oil change | Likely Cause: Routine - oil sample acceptable | Action: Drained and refilled ISO VG 220, replaced breather
- Symptom: VSHH-7802 vibration alarm on CT-7801 fan | Likely Cause: Leading-edge erosion on one FRP blade caused imbalance | Action: Inspected blades, re-balanced fan, vibration normalised
- Symptom: TSHH-7803 gearbox oil temperature rising | Likely Cause: Degraded oil and fouled oil cooler | Action: Changed oil, cleaned oil cooler, verified temperature

KEY LEARNING POINTS:
- Point 1: Low or degraded gearbox oil causes overheating (TSHH-7803) and gear failure high up on the fan deck.
- Point 2: Respect the interlock SEQ-7801: e.g. VSHH-7802 trips at > 9 mm/s - never defeat it without a permit.
- Point 3: Always cross-check the Datasheet limits and the P&ID TJC-LLD-PID-7801 before working on CT-7801.
- Point 4: Record the work in the equipment history so the Knowledge Hub stays the single source of truth.
